judged_text: poll_feed iterates the entire feed with no item cap or last-modified cutoff, and TopicEmbed.import does a fresh SELECT + SHA1 per item every hour regardless of change. A large feed causes an hourly O(N) full pass with one query per item and one PostRevisor pass per changed item on whatever single process runs the scheduled job; nothing in the design bounds the work, so feed size directly scales background cost with no pagination or batching escape hatch.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows Jobs::PollFeed is scheduled hourly and unconditionally does `rss.items.each` over the entire parsed feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) with no cap, pagination, or last-modified/ETag cutoff (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). For each item it calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and computes `Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` every time; if content changed it runs a `PostRevisor` update (app/models/topic_embed.rb). This makes the job cost scale linearly with feed size each hour and introduces one DB lookup per item, which is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect.
